title: Implement a Trie (Prefix Tree)
description: Build insert, search, and startsWith over a prefix tree, and see why it beats a hash set for prefix queries.

data.text: Implement a trie with three operations: `Insert(word)` adds a word, `Search(word)` returns whether the exact word was inserted, and `StartsWith(prefix)` returns whether any inserted word begins with the given prefix.

A `HashSet<string>` answers `Search` in O(1) but cannot answer `StartsWith` without scanning every stored word. A trie represents shared prefixes structurally, so a prefix query costs O(prefix length) regardless of how many words are stored — the property autocomplete and spell-checkers depend on.

Each node holds a dictionary from character to child node, plus a boolean flag marking whether a complete word ends here. The flag is what distinguishes the node for `"app"` in `"apple"` (not a word) from a genuine word boundary.

data.title: Trie implementation
data.content: Insert walks or creates children; search and startsWith differ only in the final check.

data.title: Search and StartsWith share one helper
data.text: Both operations walk the same path. The only difference is whether you also check `IsWord`. Factor out the walk and the two public methods become one-liners.

data.title: ArrayList-free nodes cost more memory
data.text: A 26-slot array of child pointers is faster but wastes memory on sparse nodes; a dictionary is compact but has hashing overhead and worse locality. If the alphabet is known and small, an array is often faster in practice.
Extension: Word Search in a Trie
Once you have a trie, collecting every stored word with a given prefix is a DFS from the prefix node. Adding a `List<string>` or a count to each node turns the structure into a prefix index.

data.title: Collect all words with a prefix
data.content: Walk to the prefix node, then DFS collecting every word ending below.

data.caption: After inserting apple and app, the nodes for a-p-p are shared; only the node after the second p is marked as the end of the word app.

data.title: Complete solution
data.content: The trie is the data structure behind autocomplete, IP routing tables, and the word-search-in-a-grid problem. In interviews it almost always appears in one of those three disguises rather than as a bare 'implement a trie' question.
